GET /getdata selects a users record by attacker-controlled id (JSON.parse of query param) and returns name/age/password without binding the id to authenticated identity; an attacker can read arbitrary user accounts (e.g. id 1 admin, id 2 guest).

GET /a3sensitive reads arbitrary users records via attacker-controlled id query param (parseInt) with no auth or ownership check, exposing other users' name/password/age; no predicate ties the selected object to the caller.
An HTTP response emits interpolated content as raw HTML without contextual encoding, allowing attacker markup to execute in the response's origin.

Unescaped, non-literal data is interpolated into an XPath predicate/path expression that reaches an XPath evaluator, letting an attacker change the query's grammar (predicates/node selection) instead of supplying a bound value.

POST /insecure_dor takes attacker-supplied accountno from request body and reads bank-account records (name, accounttype) from a5_insecure_dor with no authorization or ownership binding to the authenticated user; any caller can enumerate private accounts (e.g. 1001-1010).
